title: taskItemRefs still open-codes the committed-set precedence that ContractTaskIDs now delegates — add a parity guard, then fold it in
summary: core.ContractTaskIDs now delegates to internal/committedset (the one projection of the committed set: lane pin, else triage top_n, minus deferrals). Its documented parity partner core.taskItemRefs still derives the same ids inline from LaneScopeIDs + deferredTaskIDs. They agree today and a parity subtest asserts it for two fixtures, but a future change to committedset's precedence would desync them silently.
root_cause: The dossier-evidence change centralized the id projection but stopped short of taskItemRefs, whose job also includes ref/path resolution — reshaping that inside a reporting fix would have widened the diff past its thesis.
fix: First, a table-driven parity guard asserting ids(taskItemRefs(ctx, root, ws)) == ContractTaskIDs(ws) across pin/decision/deferral/empty shapes — this makes divergence loud without touching resolution logic and can land alone. Then drive taskItemRefs' id list from committedset.LanePin/DecisionTopN/Deferred, keeping the ctx fleet_scope_paths path only for PATH resolution.
acceptance: A parity test fails if taskItemRefs' id set diverges from ContractTaskIDs for any fixture in the shared table.
taskItemRefs derives its ids from committedset; ctx fleet_scope_paths is used only to resolve paths, never membership.
The Task Contract block renders identically for a lane pin, a decision-only cycle, and a deferral — pinned by existing tests; go vet + internal/core -race green.
connects_to: dossier-producer-params-struct (filed from the same review round)
notes: Raised by the architecture reviewer as MEDIUM across two rounds, explicitly non-blocking, with the parity-guard-first sequencing suggested by that reviewer.
